topic.title: Off-Policy Evaluation and Stable Temporal-Difference Learning
topic.overview: Off-policy learning uses experience collected by one policy to evaluate or improve another. This cluster studies temporal-difference updates, actor–critic algorithms, importance corrections, variance reduction, and function approximation. A representative recognizer method filters actions to create related target policies with lower-variance corrections and convergence guarantees in specified approximation settings.
topic.whyItMatters: Reusing data can make learning much more efficient, but mismatches between collection and target policies can amplify variance or destabilize updates. The same issue appears in distributed training when a rollout policy differs from the policy being optimized.
topic.evolution: Early representatives establish convergence and stable approximation in dynamic programming. Later work develops linear and doubly robust off-policy methods. Recent research connects average and discounted learning and studies sequence-level trust regions for long-horizon language-model reinforcement learning, where small local discrepancies can accumulate.
openQuestions: How can useful off-policy data be retained without unstable corrections?
Which stability guarantees survive nonlinear approximation and changing data-collection policies?

papers.tldr: The paper proves a roughly O(1/k) finite-time error rate for asynchronous average-reward Q-learning and establishes the need for adaptive step sizes in the studied algorithm.

papers.title: Offline Actor-Critic for Average Reward MDPs
papers.tldr: A pessimistic offline actor-critic algorithm achieves optimal average-reward sample complexity under a partial coverage assumption, up to model misspecification.

papers.title: On the Global Optimality of Policy Gradient Methods in General Utility Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: The paper proves global optimality results for policy gradients with concave occupancy-based utilities, including large-space methods whose sample complexity depends on representation dimension.

papers.title: Simultaneous Statistical Inference for Off-Policy Evaluation in Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: The paper constructs asymptotically valid confidence regions for off-policy evaluation that cover an entire continuous or infinite initial-state space.

papers.title: Spectral Learning for Infinite-Horizon Average-Reward POMDPs
papers.tldr: Mixed Spectral Estimation combines data from multiple belief-based policies and enables a POMDP learner with near-square-root regret under stated assumptions.

papers.title: State Entropy Regularization for Robust Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: State entropy regularization offers robustness to structured environmental changes, with benefits that depend on the setting and evaluation rollouts.

papers.title: Variance-Reduced Long-Term Rehearsal Learning with Quadratic Programming Reformulation
papers.tldr: The paper reformulates long-term undesirable-outcome avoidance as quadratic programming and develops greedy and variance-reducing far-sighted decision methods.

papers.title: Approximation of Log-Partition Function in Policy Mirror Descent Induces Implicit Regularization for LLM Post-Training
papers.tldr: PMD-mean's partition-function approximation implicitly adds adaptive regularization that helps explain its conservative, stable policy updates.

papers.title: Beyond the Bellman Recursion: A Pontryagin-Guided Framework for Non-Exponential Discounting
papers.tldr: PG-DPO uses Pontryagin-guided policy optimization to handle non-exponential discounting where standard Bellman recursions break down.

papers.title: Boosting CVaR Policy Optimization with Quantile Gradients
papers.tldr: Quantile-based updates help CVaR policy optimization use all sampled trajectories while preserving its risk-averse objective.

papers.title: Bridging the Gap Between Average and Discounted TD Learning
papers.tldr: A two-trajectory TD algorithm gives unified average-reward evaluation guarantees with improved condition-number dependence.

papers.title: Convergence of Two-Timescale Markovian Stochastic Approximations with Applications in Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: A new stability argument establishes two-timescale convergence under Markovian noise and yields an off-policy TDC convergence result.

papers.title: Error Propagation in Dynamic Programming: From Stochastic Control to American Option Pricing
papers.tldr: The paper analyzes how regression and Monte Carlo estimation errors propagate backward through dynamic programming, with an application to American option pricing.

papers.title: Finite-time Convergence Analysis of Actor-Critic with Evolving Reward
papers.tldr: Actor-critic learning can retain an O(1/√T) convergence rate when evolving rewards satisfy the paper’s assumptions and change sufficiently slowly.

papers.title: Gradient-Aware Scheduling: Coupling Curriculum and Staleness for Async Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: GAS adjusts allowable policy staleness to task difficulty, improving reported code-generation performance while increasing training throughput.

papers.title: MiniMax Learning of Interpretable Factored Stochastic Policies from Conjoint Data, with Uncertainty Quantification
papers.tldr: The paper learns interpretable strategic policies from conjoint preferences and quantifies their uncertainty under stated regularity conditions.

papers.title: Mirror Descent Actor Critic via Bounded Advantage Learning
papers.tldr: Bounding actor log-probability terms strengthens a continuous-action mirror-descent actor-critic method, with gains depending on the bounding function.

papers.title: Non-Uniform Noise-to-Signal Ratio in the REINFORCE Policy-Gradient Estimator
papers.tldr: Exact analyses in specified systems show how REINFORCE's noise relative to its learning signal can grow sharply near an optimum.

papers.title: Off-Policy Evaluation for Missingness-Aware Policies in MDPs with Rewards Missing Not at Random
papers.tldr: The paper develops policy evaluation methods that recover mean rewards under value-dependent missingness and accommodate policies that use missingness history.

papers.title: Performative Policy Gradient: Optimality in Performative Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: PePG accounts for policy-induced environment shifts and has convergence guarantees to performatively optimal policies under softmax parameterization.

papers.title: Policy Search via Bayesian Optimization with Temporal Difference Gaussian Processes
papers.tldr: Temporal-difference Gaussian processes let Bayesian policy search exploit rollout structure, with theoretical guarantees and demonstrated practical advantages.

papers.title: Refined Analysis of Entropy-Regularized Actor-Critic
papers.tldr: An exact or sufficiently accurate critic enables variance reduction and rapid convergence in the analyzed entropy-regularized actor-critic setting.

papers.title: Reusing Trajectories in Policy Gradients Enables Fast Convergence
papers.tldr: RT-PG uses corrected importance weighting to reuse past trajectories and prove faster policy-gradient convergence.

papers.title: Reward Shaping Control Variates for Off-Policy Evaluation Under Sparse Rewards
papers.tldr: Reward-shaping control variates reduce off-policy evaluation variance while preserving unbiasedness, with strong reported results under sparse rewards.

papers.title: Second-Order Smooth Planning with Optimal-Transport Bellman Smoothing
papers.tldr: Optimal-transport smoothing enables a second-order planner with ε^−3 oracle complexity for fixed smoothing parameters, improving the earlier ε^−4 dependence.

papers.title: Stable Asynchrony: Variance-Controlled Off-Policy RL for LLMs
papers.tldr: VCPO stabilizes asynchronous language-model reinforcement learning by controlling update variance using effective sample size and an off-policy baseline.

papers.title: Success-Conditioning as Policy Improvement: The Optimization Problem Solved by Imitating Success
papers.tldr: Exact success conditioning solves a data-determined trust-region problem, providing conservative policy improvement with an observable failure to progress.

papers.title: Towards Parameter-Free Temporal Difference Learning
papers.tldr: Exponential step-size schedules give TD-learning guarantees without several hard-to-estimate problem parameters, with a regularized variant for single-trajectory sampling.

papers.title: Trust Region Masking for Long-Horizon LLM Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: Trust Region Masking excludes whole sequences that violate a divergence condition, using tighter error bounds for long-horizon LLM reinforcement learning.
